9.26.8.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic. His Grace Anba Dioscorus comments on this chapter, saying that, because of the precision and clarity of this chapter in determining the time of the crucifixion of the Lord Christ after His Incarnation, the Jews changed the expression "to anoint the Most Holy" to "the dedication of the Holy of Holies" in the copy in circulation among them under the name of the Masoretic, whose date they trace to the eleventh century AD, so that the prophecy might appear to concern a place and not a person; indeed they placed the book of Daniel in the section of the Ketubim, which contains the historical books, the Psalms and the heavenly books of wisdom, so that it should not be counted among the prophetic books. This was proclaimed by some scholars.

9.26.9.en: And Fr. Bishoy Kamel comments on this prophecy, saying: [In truth these calculations gave the Jews the opportunity to know the time of the coming of the Messiah approximately. Therefore our teacher Luke the Evangelist says: "... waiting for the consolation of Israel,... redemption in Jerusalem" (Lk 2:25, 38). Indeed some thought "that the kingdom of God should immediately appear" (Lk 19:11). Therefore the Jews became without excuse in determining the time of the coming of the Lord Christ.]

9.27.s.en: Third: what is the meaning of the week?

9.27.0.en: The word "week" here came in Hebrew "shabua Shabua", derived from "seba", not in the sense of seven days, but a unit of seven. The plural of the word came "shabu'im Shabu'im", which is not the usual feminine plural of the word for week, and therefore it means sevens or periods of seven. The scholars and commentators of the Jews and Christians have agreed in their interpretation of this prophecy, despite the difference of their approaches, that the phrase "seventy weeks" means seventy units of sevens, and thus it means seventy weeks of years. The majority of commentators held that this period begins somewhere between (457 and 445 BC) and ends somewhere between (26 and 70 AD).

9.28.s.en: Fourth: the decrees concerning the return to Jerusalem and the rebuilding of the Temple and Jerusalem:

9.28.0.en: Three decrees or royal commands were issued concerning the return to Jerusalem and the rebuilding of the Temple and Jerusalem:

9.28.1.en: The first decree: issued by Cyrus in 538 BC or 537 BC, after his taking of Babylon (Isa 44:8; 45:1; Ezra 1:1-2; 2 Chr 36:22-23). The first return began under the leadership of Zerubbabel, and the restoration of the altar and the reorganization of worship began, but the enemies opposed them. In the reign of Darius I the decree of Cyrus was searched for, and the king commanded that the work continue (from 520 to 515 BC). It is fitting for us to notice that Cyrus issued a command to build the Temple only, but did not issue a command to restore the city of Jerusalem and build it. The prophet Daniel says that it is from the issuing of the command to restore Jerusalem and build it, which is different from the issuing of the command to build the Temple. There is a great difference between the two commands, for Cyrus saw no objection to helping the Jews build the Temple, as a matter of policy on his part, but he saw that helping them build the city and restore its fortifications was a danger to him. The building of the Temple is considered the end of the period of captivity, which is 70 years. The command of the king was recorded in the book of (Ezra 1:2-3): "Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, The LORD God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem." There is not a word in this command about restoring the city and building it.

9.28.2.en: The second decree: issued by King Artaxerxes I (464-424 BC) in 457 BC and carried by Ezra the priest and scribe (Ezra 8) about 80 years after the first return. The decree permitted those of the Jews who wished to return to Jerusalem (Ezra 7:13); the organization of the judiciary and the application of the law of Moses (Ezra 7:7); and the arrangement of the financial matters of the Temple (Ezra 7:15, 20). Ezra's concern was the rebuilding of the people themselves morally and spiritually (Dan 7:9). He was given the right to restore the building of the Temple and to set up the walls, for he said: "For we were bondmen; yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage, but hath extended mercy unto us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to give us a reviving, to set up the house of our God, and to repair the desolations thereof, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem" (Ezra 9:9). Unfortunately history has not given us anything about the reforms that took place concerning the building, but it is clear that Ezra carried out the moral and spiritual reform and was not able to build the walls or restore the city. This appears from what Hanani said later to Nehemiah: "The remnant that are left of the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and reproach: the wall of Jerusalem also is broken down, and the gates thereof are burned with fire" (Neh 1:3). It is clear from Nehemiah's behavior in the same chapter that he did not expect the condition of Jerusalem to be so, perhaps because he expected that Ezra and those with him had carried out restorations in the city and built the walls.

9.28.3.en: The third decree: issued by Artaxerxes I in Nisan of the twentieth year of his reign (March/April 445 BC), carried by Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer (Neh 1:11), and Nehemiah built the wall of Jerusalem and built the city, for he says to the king: "If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers' sepulchres, that I may build it" (Neh 2:5).

9.29.s.en: Fifth: the calculations of the three stages:

9.29.0.en: The prophet Daniel asked - in faith - that God fulfill His promises, which were the return of the people after seventy years of captivity; and behold, God offered him what is greater, to be accomplished not after 70 years but after its sabbaths (70 × 7 = 490 years), so that he and all mankind might enjoy a new Sabbath, and surpassing rest and the righteousness of God, which He prepared for them through the generations, and which the fathers and prophets longed for, namely the return of mankind to God through the saving work of God. This is by the Incarnation of the Word and the offering of Himself as an atonement for the sins of the world. He determined the time of the coming of this Savior and His crucifixion, as He also revealed the events of His last coming.

9.29.1.en: * This phrase stands thus, for it touches many wonders...

9.29.2.en: It is clear that the phrase speaks of the coming of Christ, who had to declare Himself after seventy weeks. For in the time of the Savior transgressions were removed and sins came to an end, and iniquities were blotted out through forgiveness, together with transgressions, by the atonement, and the everlasting righteousness, which differs from the righteousness of the Law, was preached, and the visions and prophecies (ceased) until John, and the Most Holy was anointed. For these things were not accomplished before the coming of the Savior, but they were hoping for them.

9.29.3.en: The angel teaches us that the beginning of the numbers, that is, the seventy weeks which are 490 years, begins with the command issued to begin the building of Jerusalem (in response to the request of the captives). This happened in the twentieth year of the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia. For Nehemiah asked him and received the answer that Jerusalem must be built... That was in the year 115 of the Persian Empire and the fourth year of the 83rd Olympiad, and the twentieth year of Artaxerxes himself.

9.29.4.en: To this date, which is the second year of the 202nd Olympiad and the 16th year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar (in which the Lord Christ was crucified), the sum is 475 years, which corresponds to 490 years by the Jewish reckoning, since they reckon the year according to the cycle of the moon. This is easy to show, for their year consists of 354 days while the solar year consists of 365 and a quarter days, so that the last year exceeds, in the 12 months according to the cycle of the moon, by 11 and a quarter days...

9.29.5.en: Fr. Julius Africanus: [Between the fourth year of the 83rd Olympiad and the second year of the 202nd Olympiad, where the Olympiad is held every 4 years, the sum is 475 solar years, which is equivalent to 490 lunar years.]

9.29.6.en: St. Jerome cited the opinion of Fr. Julius Africanus Julius Africanus in his interpretation of this vision.

9.30.0.en: First: 7 weeks, that is, 7×7=49 years, the period between the issuing of the command to repair the Temple and build the wall by the edict of Artaxerxes I on 14 Nisan (March - April) in the year 445 BC, and the appointment of Nehemiah as governor over Jerusalem, and the period ended in the year 397 or 396 BC, when Nehemiah died in the days of the prophet Malachi. The seven weeks [that is, 49 years] are the period of the restoration of Jerusalem and its building, because it was worn-out ruins. There is no doubt that Nehemiah spent this period in building Jerusalem, and the last of his work in his governorship over Jerusalem was the organization of the affairs of the Israelite nation and the reform of its affairs. Nehemiah was appointed governor over Judea and did not complete the restoration of Jerusalem except during the period of his second governorship. For the first time he continued 12 years as governor over Judea, because Artaxerxes issued to him a command to build Jerusalem and appointed him governor over it. And in the thirty-second year Nehemiah returned to him, then asked the king's permission to return to Jerusalem (Neh 13:6-7), and he permitted him. It is no secret that Nehemiah lived long; if his age when he began the restoration of Jerusalem was 30 years, and he spent 49 years in building it, his age was 79 years, and the historian Josephus said that he was aged.

9.30.1.en: Some give a calculation for the building of the Temple during 49 years as follows: Cyrus permitted the people to build the Temple, and they laid the foundations in three years when Cyrus went to war in Scythia Scythis, but the Jews were forced to stop building in the days of his successor Cambyses Cambyses, who was hostile to them. And when they were permitted to build, they completed it in 46 years; in this period (3 + 46 = 49 years) Jerusalem was restored, and likewise the state of the Jewish people, religiously and civilly, by Ezra and Nehemiah.

9.30.2.en: Second: 62 weeks (62 × 7 = 434 years). This period, which amounts to four centuries, represents the darkest periods of the people spiritually, for there were no prophets in it until the appearance of St. John the Baptist. They were rightly counted as sitting in darkness until the Sun of Righteousness should rise upon them by His Cross.

9.30.3.en: * After the return of the people from Babylon under the leadership of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, Ezra the scribe and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel of the tribe of David (and the restoration of Jerusalem and its building) there are 434 years until the coming of the Lord Christ, when the High Priest of priests appears to the world, and there rises clearly the One who takes away sin from the world, as John says of Him: "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world." But who is this who blots out our transgressions? Paul the Apostle teaches us, saying: "For he is our peace, who hath made both one" (Eph 2:14); and then "Blotting out the handwriting of our sins that was against us" (Col 2:14).

9.30.4.en: There are 434 years between the return of the people from Babylon (and the restoration of Jerusalem and its building) and the time of the birth of the Lord Christ. This can easily be perceived.

9.30.5.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome: In this period two important events took place:

9.30.6.en: The first event is the appearance of Antiochus Epiphanes (167-164 BC), who is considered the "antichrist" in the Old Testament, he who stopped the offering of the daily burnt sacrifice for three and a half years, and appointed Greek priests who introduced the worship of the Greek gods, and defiled the Temple with the blood of a swine and killed thousands of the Jews, but the Maccabees withstood him until the Temple was freed and the burnt offering returned.

9.30.7.en: The second event is in the days of the Roman Empire, when Herod the Great reigned, who wished to win the favor of the Jews, and began the building of the new Temple about the year 20 BC. Its building took 46 years; and he had enlarged the Temple area to nearly double the space.

9.31.0.en: Since it is stated in [27] that the abolition of the animal sacrifice is in the midst of the week, that is, in the midst of the last week of the 69 weeks, this means that the crucifixion takes place in week 68.5, that is, after (68.5 × 7) 479.5 years from the issuing of the edict for the work of restoring the Temple by Nehemiah (in 445 BC), so that the crucifixion is 33 and a half years after the birth, and this was fulfilled, for the Lord Christ was crucified at this age. As for the end of the last week, it is about 35 years after the crucifixion (3.5 days), that is, about the year 70 AD, when the Temple was completely demolished at the hands of Titus the Roman.

9.31.1.en: Some scholars hold that the crucifixion of the Lord Christ came 483 years (7 + 62 = 69 × 7 = 483) after the issuing of the edict of Artaxerxes mentioned above. Because the crucifixion took place in April of the year 30 AD, if the edict was issued in 445 BC, the difference is 445 BC + 30 = 475 years and not 483, so there is a difference of 8 years. The reason for these eight years is that the year in the Holy Bible is reckoned as 360 days and not like the astronomical or Julian year of 365 and a quarter days. The five and a quarter days in the year cause a difference of 8 years. Thus the coming of the Messiah the Prince was fulfilled exactly after 69 weeks (69 × 7 = 483 years), reckoning the year as it is in the Holy Bible.

9.31.2.en: Gleason L. Archer holds that the 69 symbolic years (483 years) are reckoned from the second decree, or the first decree with respect to King Artaxerxes I in 457 BC, which was carried by Ezra the scribe for the building, even though the building was accomplished only by Nehemiah. If we subtract 483 from 457 BC, 26 remains, and since there is no year equal to zero, the number 1 is added to 26, so that the date is 27 AD. And since it is known that the Lord Christ was crucified in 30 AD, He would have begun His ministry and His baptism in 27 AD. Thus the prophecy was fulfilled exactly.

9.31.3.en: Others hold that the twentieth year of Artaxerxes is the year 454 BC, according to the investigations of the scholars Hengstenberg and Ussher. If we subtract this period from the product of 69 weeks multiplied by 7 (483 years), which is the period the prophet Daniel spoke of in verse 25, the remainder is about 29 AD, which is the beginning of the ministry of the Lord Christ, or His call to the way of salvation, for it is the very goal intended, because the important point in the dates of kings and sultans is the beginning of their reign and work, and not their birth; therefore the prophet Daniel observed this very point that was intended.

9.31.4.en: Thus many hold that this second period ends with the baptism of the Lord Christ and the beginning of His preaching of His Gospel, so that the third period comes, in which the Lord Christ offers His sacrifice in the midst of the week, that is, after three and a half years of His ministry, and the animal sacrifices are abolished.

9.32.s.en: Third: the seventieth week, or the last week.

9.32.0.en: "And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease..." [27].

9.32.1.en: There is an opinion or meditation in the interpretation of this verse that this week refers to the week of the Passion with its seven days, when the Lord Christ entered the Temple on Sunday (the tenth of Nisan) as a lamb and drove out the sheep that symbolized Him, and continued to stay overnight in Bethany as though under guard until the fourteenth day (Thursday), when He kept the last Passover with His disciples and abolished it, and it was the supper at which He offered to His disciples the sacrifice of the New Covenant, with His Body and Blood changed from the bread and wine, as a rite after the order of Melchizedek according to the prophecy of the prophet David in the Psalm. The first five days refer to the five thousand years (approximately) in which the bloody sacrifices that symbolized Him were offered, then the remaining two days of the week to the two thousand years, and thus the saying of Peter the Apostle is fulfilled when he speaks of the second coming of the Lord Christ for judgment, saying: "But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.. etc." (2 Pet 3:8-10).

9.32.2.en: Some hold that the 69 weeks ended with the Lord Christ's offering of Himself as a unique sacrifice of love, and now the vision of Daniel carries us to the end of the world, which is the period of the last seven years in which the Antichrist comes to reign for three and a half years, when there is the great tribulation of which the Lord Christ spoke: "When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:) Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains: Let him which is on the housetop not come down to take any thing out of his house... For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be. And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened (Mt 24:15-21). And He spoke after that of His last coming.

9.32.3.en: Daniel also spoke of it in another place: "and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time" (Dan 12:1). And in Jeremiah: "Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it" (Jer 30:7); and it is stated in Zephaniah: "Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy" (Zeph 1:18).

9.32.4.en: And it is stated in the book of Revelation: "These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb" (Rev 7:14). The description of this period of tribulation is given in (Rev 6:15; 11:1-14; 12:6-17).

9.32.5.en: * By the stretching out of His hands he means His sufferings, and by the reference to a time, times and half a time he indicates the three and a half years of the Antichrist... which are the 1290 days that Daniel prophesied for the ending of the suffering and the accomplishment of the scattering when the Antichrist comes.

9.32.7.en: You grant me more than I ask,
